entry_points: dependency_closure(seed_ids, edges, direction, max_depth, max_nodes, max_edges, authoritative_only, edge_kinds) -> dict
CodeEvidenceCorpusAdapter.dependency_query(family, seed_ids, direction, max_depth, authoritative_only, edge_kinds) -> dict
identity_and_determinism: Graph and semantic-graph normalization sorts nodes and edges by their canonical identifiers before graph identities are derived; graph IDs are content identities over canonical payloads.

dependency_closure normalizes seeds by text and lexical sort, records shortest lexical tie-broken paths, returns sorted node IDs, paths, and depths, and is bounded by max_depth, max_nodes, and max_edges.
For reverse traversal, the selected authority follows target-to-source edges, producing dependents rather than falsely treating reverse impact as a forward dependency slice.

impact_from_index constructs reverse symbol and path maps, returns sorted affected symbols/paths and validation IDs, preserves dependency chains, and marks uncovered symbols or paths rather than silently claiming complete impact.

The query is identity-bound to the selected graph_id/root_id or impact index_id and repository_tree_id supplied by the canonical loaded artifact. No CID is claimed where the authority exposes a graph/index content identity instead.
fail_closed_invariants: Invalid direction, negative bounds, empty seeds, max-edge overflow, and max-node overflow raise CodeEvidenceAdapterError.
authoritative_only excludes non-authoritative edges; edge_kinds restricts traversal to an explicit allowlist.
Missing, corrupt, checksum-mismatched, or forged graph artifacts fail before their graph/index can be selected for slicing.
Unknown changed symbols and paths remain explicitly uncovered_impact rather than being converted into a complete slice.
